# Can pre-call data rank likely responses?

I used the date-ordered [UCI Bank Marketing dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/222/bank+marketing) (CC BY 4.0) to evaluate a logistic model against a constant-prevalence baseline. I excluded call duration because it is unknown before the call. The [reproducible code](https://github.com/nandinnnnnnnnnnnn/Portfolio-page/tree/main/projects/bank-response-model) selects regularization on a later validation segment and tests once on the latest 20%.

![Held-out precision-recall curve](bank-response-model/outputs/precision_recall.svg)

On **8,238** held-out rows, average precision was **0.5383** for logistic regression and **0.3083** for the constant baseline. ROC AUC was **0.7012** versus **0.5000**. The top-scored 10% contained **547** positives among **824** records.

The positive rate changed from **4.79%** in training to **12.72%** in validation and **30.83%** in test. Exact dates, customer IDs, and costs are unavailable, so these are retrospective ranking results, not a contact policy or business lift estimate. [Read the full case study](https://github.com/nandinnnnnnnnnnnn/Portfolio-page/blob/main/projects/bank-response-model/CASE_STUDY.md).
